_what: Example of McpServer/OutlookAI.McpServer.Tests/live-fixtures/live-test-settings.json, which is gitignored and must stay that way - it names real stores and this repository is public. Copy this file there and replace every value. Keys are matched case-insensitively and unknown keys are ignored, so the _-prefixed notes below are safe to keep or delete.
_shape: This is the PORTABLE (test-VM) shape. A Production profile additionally REQUIRES 'probeTerm' (a word proven to hit that machine's search index) and a complete 'subjectOnlyProbe' block { storeDisplayName, folderPath, subjectTerm, senderFragment }, and may carry an optional 'delegateNestedFolderProbe' block { storeDisplayName, folderName, comParentPath }. They are left out here on purpose: a test machine has no such populations, and inventing plausible values is worse than omitting them because the failures then land far from the mistake.
_partialBlocksAreRejected: corpus, mailSink and subjectOnlyProbe are all-or-nothing. A block with three fields out of four reads as configured and behaves as absent, which is exactly the silence these checks exist to remove - so the loader throws instead.
_bystanders: The stores the count tripwire exists to watch: watched, and written to by NOTHING. Naming a store here denies it every kind of write, keeps it in the census, and takes it out of the identity tests' account list - so it must ALSO stay in expectedStoreDisplayNames above, which is what gets it censused and counted by list_accounts. Without this list the bystander was inside the identity-draft grant purely by being a non-hub primary, and a store the suite may write to cannot be evidence of anything. Naming the hub here is refused at the top of the run, not resolved. On a Production profile the delegate mailboxes are already denied and already watched, so they need no declaration.
_bystandersAreMANDATORY: The live tier REFUSES to start when this leaves the census nothing it could fail on - no watched store that is both non-hub and denied every write. There is no flag that turns that refusal off. It is not a formality: the run it used to allow censused every folder, identified nothing and printed '0 failure(s)' whatever had happened to the mail. If the refusal fires it names the two keys to edit.
_corpusStoresAreBystandersToo: The measurement corpus store is declared here as well, and it matters more than it looks. No live test writes to a corpus: LiveCorpusFreshness only reads the manifest, and re-anchoring is an operator action from the accountless profile. Left undeclared, a corpus store listed in expectedStoreDisplayNames is inside the identity-draft grant purely for being a non-hub primary - so the identity tests would create drafts in the measurement corpus the moment this machine gains a mail account, and the post-run artifact sweep, which matches on the [OutlookAI-McpTest] tag that every corpus subject also carries, would try to DELETE the corpus. Declaring it makes both a refusal instead. Declare only corpus stores THIS Outlook profile actually mounts: a declared store the profile does not have is watched, cannot be censused, and refuses the tier. Corpus B lives in the other Windows account's profile per Docs/live-tier-on-the-vm.md section 1.1, so it belongs in THAT machine's settings file, declared the same way - not here.

corpus._note: The four identity values must match Testbed/testbed.json. manifestPath is machine-local and is the ONLY thing that can tear the corpus down - keep a copy outside the guest.

mailSink._note: Loopback submission and retrieval. Absent means this machine has real transport. Ports are whatever the sink was configured with; nothing needs the well-known numbers. See Testbed/README.md question 11 before assuming the retrieval side is POP3.
